skill.summary: Request public NetEase Cloud Music data through Apify using documented inputs and a Node.js runner.

security_audit.summary: All 63 static alerts are false positives in context: formatting, JavaScript strings, intended input reads, documented Apify requests, and expected credential access. No evidence found of prompt injection, shell injection, credential theft, or unauthorized file traversal in the reviewed files. The remote Actor implementation is not bundled, so its behavior was not independently verified.

content.user_title: Collect NetEase Cloud Music Catalog and Chart Data
content.value_statement: Public NetEase Cloud Music research requires consistent catalog, playlist, and chart records. This skill provides documented Apify inputs and a Node.js runner for requesting structured datasets.
actual_capabilities: Submit song, album, artist, or playlist searches through the documented Apify Actor.
Configure song, album, artist catalog, and artist discography requests using URLs, IDs, or supported names.
Configure playlist category browsing and playlist tracklist requests.
Request chart catalogs or chart tracks with per-chart and total record limits.
Configure public comment collection, optional replies, lyrics, and artist profiles through documented input options.
Run synchronous requests with Node.js and print JSON results, or follow documented curl commands for asynchronous dataset retrieval.
limitations: Scraping runs in an external Apify Actor; its implementation is not bundled, and live output was not verified during this audit.
Execution requires an Apify token and billable service access; the bundled runner also requires Node.js 18 or later.
The documented scope excludes private, login-protected, and paywalled data; anonymous comment pagination is limited to about 1,100 top-level comments.
The runner prints JSON, not CSV, and does not locally validate the Actor input schema; returned fields can vary by mode.

use_cases.title: Explore public playlists

use_cases.title: Build catalog data feeds
use_cases.description: Request song and artist catalog records as JSON inputs for downstream data processing.

prompt_templates.title: Search for songs
prompt_templates.prompt: Search NetEase Cloud Music for songs matching [query]. Set mode to search, searchType to song, and maxItems to 25. Summarize available names, artists, and albums.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: a small public catalog search

prompt_templates.title: Inspect selected songs
prompt_templates.prompt: Request details for [public song URLs] using mode bySongUrl. Enable includeLyrics and cap maxItems at 10. Report available metadata and identify missing fields.

prompt_templates.title: Review playlist tracklists
prompt_templates.prompt: Request [public playlist URLs] using mode byPlaylistUrl and includePlaylistTracks. Set maxItems to 100. Group available track names, artists, and durations by playlist.

prompt_templates.title: Export chart datasets asynchronously
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an asynchronous Apify run for [chart IDs] using mode byToplist. Set maxTracksPerChart to 50 and maxItems to 200. Confirm cost approval before starting. Wait for terminal success before downloading the dataset. Summarize available chart names, ranks, tracks, and source URLs.

output_examples.input: Search for songs matching [query], limited to 25 records.
output: Illustrative layout only; no live query was performed.

output_examples.input: Request the first 10 tracks from [chart ID].
output: Illustrative layout only; no live chart was retrieved.

best_practices: Start with maxItems set to 25 and confirm current Apify pricing before increasing limits.
Keep APIFY_TOKEN in the environment and send only approved public-data inputs to the remote service.
Check input options, terminal run status, returned record types, and source-site terms before integrating or redistributing results.
anti_patterns: Do not submit cookies, sessions, private account information, or unrelated local JSON files.
Do not assume a successful HTTP response guarantees complete results or every documented output field.
Do not launch broad chart or comment collection without explicit limits and cost approval.

faq.question: Does this skill scrape NetEase locally?
faq.answer: No. The local runner sends inputs to an external Apify Actor and prints the returned dataset.

faq.question: Which credentials and runtime are required?
faq.answer: Set APIFY_TOKEN for an authorized Apify account. The bundled runner requires Node.js 18 or later; documented curl examples provide another execution method.

faq.question: Which public resources can I request?
faq.answer: The input schema documents songs, artists, albums, playlists, charts, and comments, with optional lyrics, replies, and artist profiles.

faq.question: Can I retrieve private data or download audio?
faq.answer: Private, login-protected, and paywalled data are excluded. No audio download capability is documented.

faq.question: Does the runner export CSV?
faq.answer: No. It prints JSON results. CSV conversion requires a separate processing step.

faq.question: How should I handle larger runs?
faq.answer: Use the documented asynchronous API workflow and explicit record limits. Confirm terminal success before retrieving results, and review current Apify charges.
